title: Reseller Catalogue for WhatsApp Sellers | OneCatalog
description: A reseller catalogue with your own prices and your own WhatsApp number. Share one link instead of forwarding supplier photos to every buyer.
h1: A reseller catalogue with your prices, not your supplier's
answer: A reseller catalogue is one link that shows the products you resell, at the price you set, with your WhatsApp number on every product. OneCatalog builds it from the supplier photos you pick. Your buyers see a clean catalogue under your own name, not a pile of forwarded photos.
sub: Your shop name. Your prices. Your buyers message you, not your supplier.
waText: Hi OneCatalog, I am a reseller and want a catalogue.

mockup.label: Sample reseller catalogue with the reseller's own prices, shown on a phone

sections.h2: Why forwarding supplier photos stops working

blocks.p: Take a reseller who works from home in Surat. Her suppliers send 40 new product photos a day. She forwards the good ones to her buyer groups. She changes the price in each caption. Then she answers the same questions all evening.

pain: Forwarded photos often show the supplier's price or logo, not yours.
Buyers see the same product from five resellers in one group, and they pick the cheapest.
Nobody can scroll back and find the kurti from last Tuesday.

blocks.p: If you resell on apps like Meesho, you know this well. A catalogue gives you a shop window that is your own, and it stays put.

You pick the products you want to sell. You send us the photos with your selling price. We build a catalogue under your shop name, with your WhatsApp number on every Enquire button. Your margin is already inside the price your buyer sees.

steps.title: Pick your products
steps.text: Choose the items you want to sell and send us the photos with your price for each one.

steps.title: We build your catalogue
steps.text: In 48 hours you get a link like yourshop.onecatalog.in, with your name at the top.

steps.title: Share and take orders
steps.text: Buyers open the link, look around and message you. You order from your supplier the way you do today.

sections.h2: Is a catalogue right for my reselling?

blocks.p: Think about how fast your products change. Every plan includes 12 update requests a year, each for up to 10 products. Extra batches cost ₹299 for 10 products.

sections.h2: Choose products that sell again and again

blocks.p: Your supplier may send you hundreds of products. You do not need all of them in your catalogue. The best reseller catalogues are small and careful.

ul: Start with the 20 products your buyers ask about most. These are your proven sellers.
Pick items that your supplier keeps in stock for months, not days.
Group them the way your buyers shop, like kurtis, bedsheets and kitchen items.
Leave out items that every other reseller in your group is already sharing. Show the ones that make you different.

sections.h2: Build trust as a home reseller

blocks.p: New buyers often wonder if a reseller is real. A catalogue helps. It has your shop name, your WhatsApp number and an About page about you. That looks much more serious than a forwarded photo.

ul: Tell us a few lines about yourself for your About page, like your city and how long you have been selling.
Add one or two real photos of products you have at home. Real photos in daylight build more trust than studio photos.
Use the same shop name everywhere, in your catalogue, your WhatsApp profile and your groups.

head: Category
Details shown

blocks.p: Ask your supplier for photos without their price or logo. Clean photos make your catalogue look like your own shop.

ul: Pick supplier photos with a plain background. Mixed backgrounds make the catalogue look messy.
Skip photos that have text or prices printed on them.
Choose one main photo and one close photo for each product. Ten angles is too many.
If you have the product at home, one real photo in daylight works better than a studio photo.

blocks.p: Resellers with a short list start on Lite. It costs ₹1,999 a year for up to 20 products, on a onecatalog.in link. If you have more products or want your own domain, pick up to 50 products for ₹3,999 in the first year. See every plan on the [pricing page](/pricing). Our [WhatsApp catalogue page](/whatsapp-catalogue) shows how to share the link. If you resell clothing, the [garment catalogue page](/catalogue-maker/garments) has more ideas.

items.q: Can I set my own price with my margin?
items.a: Yes. You send us your selling price for each product. That is the only price your buyers see.

items.q: Will my supplier's name show anywhere?
items.a: No. The catalogue shows your shop name and your WhatsApp number. Use photos without the supplier's logo.

items.q: Can I share my catalogue link in WhatsApp groups?
items.a: Yes. Share the main link, or a link to one product, in any group, chat, status or broadcast list.

items.q: What happens when my supplier runs out of a product?
items.a: Tell us and we mark it out of stock. The product stays in your catalogue with a badge, so buyers know it is not available right now. When it is back, we remove the badge. Each change counts towards your included update requests.
Yes. The Lite plan is for up to 20 products at ₹1,999 a year. Many resellers start there and move up when they add more products.

items.q: What will my link look like?
items.a: On Lite it looks like yourshop.onecatalog.in. On plans from ₹3,999, you can have your own domain, registered in your business name.

items.q: Can I change my prices later?
items.a: Yes. Send the new prices on WhatsApp and we update them. Price changes use your included update requests, 12 a year of up to 10 products each.

items.q: Can buyers pay inside the catalogue?
items.a: No. There is no cart or online payment. Buyers message you on WhatsApp, and you take payment the way you do today.
You do, the same way as now. The catalogue only shows your products and sends buyers to your WhatsApp.

items.q: Do I need a GST number to get a catalogue?
items.a: No. A catalogue is a website that shows your products. Your accountant can tell you if your reselling needs GST.
No. OneCatalog is a separate service. It is not linked to any reselling app.

items.q: Do my buyers need an app to see my catalogue?
items.a: No. It opens in the browser on any phone. They only need WhatsApp to message you.
